subject: Service reliability measurement and dashboard access — procurement questions
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-18 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement questionnaire — reliability metrics and monitoring access

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking time with Acme Procurement. We're wrapping up the SOW review and the procurement team has a short set of questions we need answered for our security and procurement checklist related to reliability commitments. Can you please provide brief answers to the items below? We want to make sure the contract reflects operational reality.

1) What uptime SLA do you commit to for the Hosted API (monthly uptime percentage)? How do you calculate the measurement window (UTC rolling 30-day, calendar month, other)?
2) For latency commitments, what percentiles and endpoints are covered (p50/p95/p99 for text generation vs embeddings)? Are these end-to-end (including network) or server-side only?
3) How are incidents/maintenance windows treated against SLA calculation (planned maintenance exclusions, emergency maintenance, customer-requested upgrades)?
4) What monitoring/metrics access will Acme receive? Can we get read-only Grafana dashboards or an API for aggregator metrics? Any restrictions?
5) Alerting: Will Acme be able to configure per-route alerts or subscribe to our PagerDuty? What alert channels are supported?
6) Data retention for telemetry / request logs used for SLO verification—how long are these retained and what is the process to request exports for audits?

We're aiming to finalize the procurement checklist by next Thursday (2027-04-22). If you can respond with a primary answer and attach any short docs or example queries, that would be great.

Best,
Daniel
Procurement Lead, Acme Corp

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Answers below are high-level; I flagged a couple of items for our infra team to add technical detail. I attached a short SLO definition doc and example query snippets.

1) Uptime SLA: Redwood offers a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA for the Hosted API (post-commissioning availability). We measure uptime over a rolling 30-day UTC window by default and report on calendar-month on request for billing/credit calculations.

2) Latency commitments: We publish p50/p95/p99 for primary inference endpoints (text generation and embeddings) measured server-side (end of runtime before egress). Typical published commitments: text generation p95 < 350ms for standard models, embeddings p95 < 80ms. We can include end-to-end network timings in a separately tracked report if Acme prefers.

3) Incidents/maintenance: Planned maintenance (with >48h notice) is excluded from SLA calculations for the maintenance window. Emergency maintenance (security patches) is handled case-by-case — short emergency windows are typically not excluded; however, for enterprise contracts we can negotiate limited exclusions. Customer-initiated scheduled downtime (e.g., model migration requested by customer) is excluded.

4) Monitoring/metrics access: Acme will receive read-only Grafana dashboard access scoped to your account plus ingestion of key SLO timeseries via a metrics API. Access is governed by RBAC — we can provide dashboard links and invite two SRE contacts by default.

5) Alerting: We support integration with PagerDuty and Slack. Acme can configure per-route alerts for error rate, latency breach, and sustained degradation. Alert rules are editable by Account Admins; we also offer an optional managed alerting subscription for joint triage.

6) Telemetry retention: Service telemetry (per-request logs used for SLO verification) is retained for 13 months by default. Export requests for audits are fulfilled via secure export (SFTP or signed link) within 7 business days; shorter SLAs can be negotiated.

I've looped in Vivek (infra) and Karthik (sales) to confirm the technical queries and to arrange Grafana invites. Attaching: redwood-slo-definition.pdf and example-slo-queries.txt.

Thanks — happy to iterate.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Director, GTM Engineering | Redwood Inference

Daniel — quick technical clarifications from infra below and a link to an invite.

- SLA calc: uptime is computed from service health check series (per-region front door + per-model serving fleet) aggregated to a single account-level availability metric; rolling 30d window uses sliding-window approach with per-minute resolution.
- Latency: the published p95/p99 are server-side ; we can provide a companion end-to-end ping test for your agents.
- Maintenance: we maintain a public maintenance calendar for customers with enterprise contracts. Planned maintenance windows are excluded only for the exact scheduled minutes. If a maintenance overruns we provide incident records and reconciliations.
- Monitoring access: I'm sending a one-time Grafana invite (see attached: grafana-invite.txt). The invite gives read-only role and a separate service token can be provisioned for API pulls. Please confirm the two SRE emails you want invited.
- Example query: included in example-slo-queries.txt — shows how we compute 99.9% uptime from per-minute availability series and the alerting rule used for sustained degradation (30m sliding window > 0.5% error budget burn).

Notes on exception requests: If Acme needs a formal exception for a maintenance-heavy migration, procurement should request an SLA exception; this request will be reviewed by Product+Infra and documented (timeboxed).

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Please invite these two SRE addresses for read-only Grafana: sre-acme-1@acme.com, sre-acme-2@acme.com.
- We'd like to see a sample incident report you provide after maintenance overruns (anonymized is fine) to confirm reconciliation detail.
- For the telemetry export SLA: can Redwood support CSV export and MD5-signed bundles for chain-of-custody? We may need exports sooner than 7 business days for audits.
- Finally, Acme's security policy requires a 30-day notice for SLA exception approvals (for major scheduled migrations). Are you able to accept that notice period?

If you can reply with the invite + sample incident report by EOD tomorrow, we can clear procurement sign-off.

Thanks,
Lena
